findings.where: 'Where we're starting' section: the Canggu, Uluwatu and Kuta Lombok destination cards with their 'Best hostels >' lines, reached from the hero's 'Explore destinations' button and the nav's 'Destinations' link
findings.fault: The cards look clickable: each has a white card, an arrow, link-coloured text and a hover rule. But none of them goes anywhere (parts p8 to p10 are static). Both routes to the guides scroll down to cards that lead nowhere, so the page fails one of its three jobs, sending visitors to the destination guides.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker planning their next stop in Bali or Lombok. They follow 'Explore destinations', tap 'Best hostels' and nothing happens. They leave thinking the site is broken or empty, which also makes them less likely to sign up for launch news.

findings.where: 'How we rank' in the top nav and in the footer
findings.fault: The page's main claim is that it ranks hostels 'on merit alone', and 'How we rank' is the one link that should back that up. Both copies of the link just reload this page, so the proof is promised and never delivered. A merit claim with an explanation link that goes nowhere reads as empty marketing.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker who has learned not to trust ranking sites, since they know OTAs sell placement. Merit ranking is the reason to care about Manta, so this is exactly the link they click, and finding nothing confirms their suspicion.

findings.where: Footer links: Privacy, Terms, Report content
findings.fault: The page asks for the visitor's email address, but Privacy, Terms and Report content all just reload the homepage. There is nothing that says what happens to their address. Legal links that lead nowhere are a classic sign of a placeholder or fly-by-night site.
findings.who_objects: A careful first-time visitor, especially an EU or UK traveller, who checks the privacy link before giving an email to an unknown pre-launch site. They find no policy and don't sign up.

findings.where: Hero: the coral 'Email luc@mantahostels.com for launch news' button
findings.fault: The only way to sign up is a mailto link. The visitor has to leave the page, open a mail app (on a shared or desktop computer there may not be one set up) and work out what to write. Nothing next to the button says what they will get, how often, or that their address won't be shared or used for anything else. With the high effort and no reassurance, many will give up halfway.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker on a phone in transit, often on a poor connection, who would gladly leave an address but won't stop to compose an email to a stranger with no idea what they're signing up for.

findings.where: Hero: the line above the wordmark, 'The better way to find hostels in Indonesia.'
findings.fault: The headline promise is a vague comparative ('better') that names no benefit to the traveller. The page's real benefit, finding the right hostel faster, never appears. The body text gives the mechanism (merit ranking, booking direct) but not why the traveller gains from it, so the 5-second test answers 'what' and not 'why should I care'.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker who already uses Hostelworld or Booking.com and reads 'better' as filler. Nothing tells them what they would gain by switching.

findings.where: Whole page: hero copy ('We're building'), the footer line 'Launching across Indonesia · piloting now in Bali', and the Lombok card under 'Where we're starting'
findings.fault: The page gives mixed signals about what is live and when. The hero says the search is still being built, while the footer says it is 'piloting now', which implies something can be used today. The footer says the pilot is in Bali, yet one of the starting destinations is in Lombok. There is no launch date or season, and no copyright year, so nothing shows the site is current or says when the 'launch news' will come.
findings.who_objects: A visitor deciding whether to sign up or come back. They can't tell whether there is anything to use now or how long they'd wait, and the contradictions make the operation look less organised than it is.

findings.where: Hero and footer: who is behind MantaHostels
findings.fault: The only hint of a person behind the site is the first name in an email address. No line names the founder or says it is an independent, one-person project based in Indonesia or anywhere else. For a pre-launch site asking for an email and claiming independent ranking, the lack of a named owner makes it feel anonymous.
findings.who_objects: A wary traveller, and any hostel owner who comes across the page, who wants to know who is making the merit-ranking promise and whether that person is independent of the booking sites.

findings.where: Whole page, next to the launch-news sign-up
findings.fault: There is no third-party proof of any kind near the sign-up. The project has none to show, and inventing any is forbidden, so this gap is noted, not something to fill with made-up proof.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor weighing whether to hand an email to an unknown brand. Nothing outside Manta's own words vouches for it.
